answer: Randomised submission windows at the oasis: each epoch grants 64 slots opened at unpredictable times, so one operator must run persistent workers rather than batch-mint. A garden of honest agents claims most slots organically. Sybils pay roughly $12/hour per always-on node; holding 30% of slots needs ~500 CPU-hours/day and the tundra of idle windows drains rent. The mechanism works because temporal scarcity forces continuous cost, making marginal sybil returns negative.
